summary: trades.py: max_fee keyword with default_max_fee(price) = ceil(25%); buy completes only with exactly the requested quantity and payment within [price, price+max_fee], and a still-open targeted listing makes it unknown; sell proceeds must arrive at/after ListingGone within [price-max_fee, price]; sale ids seen before the request never match, listing quantity must match when given, and several matching sale ids give requested with an ambiguity reason. ledger.py: actions starting inside an interval and overlapping its end are candidates (ambiguous with others), except when a later snapshot falls inside their window (the runner's own pair), keeping inter-run gaps unattributed; a two-run runner round trip confirms. Regression tests fail on the old code. Implemented by a subagent in a worktree; re-validated by the parent.

contract_status_changes.before: Trades completed from unrelated item and currency movements; ledger changes could be credited to the wrong action
contract_status_changes.after: Trades complete only with bounded, correctly timed movements and an unambiguous listing; end-overlapping actions make attribution ambiguous
proof: reviewer repro now gives ambiguous / unknown / unknown
regression tests fail on the previous code and pass now

residual_risks: A real sale whose proceeds arrive before the ListingGone poll now reconciles as unknown (stricter by design).
The 25% default fee bound is an assumption; the game's actual market fee is unverified.
